meta.title: Clean b/ub doubling sweep on 1660 Super
meta.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 SUPER (CUDA1, 6 GB, MMQ-only, cc 7.5, no tensor cores)

matched_pair_sweep_b_equals_ub.description: b=ub matched pair doubling sweep per task spec

b256_ub256.detail: exit code 9 - model too large for 6 GB VRAM with ub=256

matched_pair_sweep_b_equals_ub.conclusion: Matched-pair sweep stopped at b=128 (b256/ub256 OOM). Optimal matched pair: b=128, ub=128.

extended_sweep_ub128_fixed.description: Extended sweep with ub=128 fixed (prior baseline showed this is optimal ubatch)

b256_ub128.detail: Below 5% threshold from b128 peak (24.30 * 0.95 = 23.09). Would stop here per sweep rules.

b512_ub128.detail: New peak! ub=128 allows b=512 to fit within 6 GB

conclusions: Matched-pair (b=ub) sweep: b=128/ub=128 peak at 24.30 t/s; b=256/ub=256 OOM on 6GB card
Extended with ub=128 fixed: b=512/ub=128 gives 25.43 t/s (+4.6% vs b=128/ub=128)
GTX 1660 Super (6GB MMQ-only) can only handle ub=128 at higher batch sizes
Optimal config for this GPU: b=512, ub=128 (matches prior baseline)
PP speed stable at ~114 t/s across all tested configs
TG limited by MMQ kernel performance on cc 7.5 GPU without tensor cores
